reproducedDefects.missingAnimation: The actual HUD consumes a new seq while now is one simulation tick earlier than the kill's at timestamp. ul rejects a negative age and the HUD permanently clears its active flag. A regression using at=10 and now=10-1/128 fails before the patch and recovers after clamping the age to zero.
reproducedDefects.missingLowerRightQuadrant: The actual expiry clear uses the translated/scaled context left by the previous draw. clearRect(0,0,width,height) therefore only erases the right-bottom region. The regression records the old matrix [0.55,0,0,0.55,150,150]; the fix resets to identity before clearing the entire backing canvas.

newCoverage: An early-timestamp kill remains active until the HUD clock catches up.
Expiry clears in backing-pixel coordinates after a transformed draw.
All four Ayakashi variants use distinct original RGBA sources and the reviewed flame sprite rectangle, with no generic fallback.
Out-of-bounds sprite geometry is rejected before replacing previous media output.

browserLifecycleReview.method: A temporary isolated localhost page imports the delivered skin runtime and executes the actual KillBannerHud component plus its native animation/placement functions extracted from delivered DVK7uRSu.js. Each test submits a kill one tick ahead of the HUD clock, advances to 250ms, checks actual nonzero pixels in all four quadrants, jumps beyond expiry while skipping the fade, and checks that every quadrant is completely transparent.
browserLifecycleReview.manualLiveKills: Not exercised; actual HUD events, animation and pixel output are exercised by this browser harness.

limitations: Ayakashi flames are sampled from original transparent composites, not independently unpacked game textures. Original Unreal shader/VFX animation is not reproduced.
